label: TMUA 2022 · Paper 2 · Question 6

hints.title: Keep the two directions separate
hints.body: P says the number of entries is odd. Q says the median is an entry of the list. Sufficiency asks whether P forces Q; necessity asks whether Q forces P.
hints.recap: Test P⇒Q and Q⇒P as different claims.
hints.pitfall: Do not swap the meanings of necessary and sufficient.
hints.pause: What does an odd number of sorted entries guarantee about the middle?

recall.reminder: A condition is sufficient if it implies the target; it is necessary if the target implies it.

hints.title: Apply the median definition
hints.body: For an odd-length sorted list, the median is its single middle entry. For an even-length sorted list, it is the average of the two middle entries. Apply these definitions to the two statements in the question.
hints.recap: Sort the list before locating its middle position or positions.
hints.pitfall: The question asks whether the median occurs in the list, not merely whether it is an integer.
hints.pause: Decide what follows from odd length, then investigate whether the reverse implication must also hold.

recall.reminder: Use the odd-length and even-length median definitions, and test each implication separately.

hints.title: Investigate the even-length cases
hints.body: Try permitted even-length lists, including examples with distinct entries and examples with repetitions. Calculate each median and check whether it is actually an entry of that list.
hints.recap: For even length, the median is the average of the two middle entries.
hints.pitfall: An integer median is not enough: the question asks whether that value occurs in the list.
hints.pause: Produce a proof or a valid counterexample for the reverse implication, then combine the two directions.

recall.reminder: Test the reverse implication separately using objects that satisfy its own hypothesis.

solution:
Suppose P holds. After sorting an odd number of entries, there is a single middle entry. That entry is the median, so Q follows. Thus P is sufficient for Q.

To test necessity, use the permitted list 2,2. Its median is 2, an entry of the list, but its length is even. Therefore Q does not imply P, and P is not necessary for Q.

P is sufficient but not necessary for Q: C. The counterexample is allowed because repeated integers were not excluded.
knowledgePattern: Odd-length median sufficiency versus repeated middle values
